newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA'S VOLKSWAGEN SAYS STRIKE OVER.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA'S VOLKSWAGEN SAYS STRIKE OVER.

text.p: German automaker Volkswagen's plant in South Africa's Eastern Cape would begin normal operations on Tuesday after an illegal strike by employees ended on Monday, the company said in a statement.
Volkswagen said National Union of Metalworkers of South Africa (Numsa) representatives informed it that union members had agreed to return to work.
The company earlier obtained an interim interdict from the Labour Court declaring the strike illegal which meant that strikers were not protected from dismissal.
"Volkswagen of South Africa's Uitenhage plant will reopen for normal production tomorrow (Tuesday), following agreement with the National Union of Metalworkers of South Africa.
"Numsa officials informed (Volkswagen) management today (Monday) that union members had agreed to end their strike and return to work," the company added.
The Uitenhage plant was officially closed last Thursday and work remained halted last Friday. Last week's stoppage followed close on the heels of a three-day strike the previous week.
Workers last week were protesting against the company's cost-cutting measures and its move to discipline two colleagues in connection with the strike which started on March 18.
Volkswagen warned that the strike had had "a very negative" impact on the company's financial performance.
The Uitenhage plant produces around 320 vehicles a day valued at about 16 million rand, the company said.
The company said that the illegal strike action had been undertaken by a small minority of the company's approximate 4,000 hourly-rated employees.

"Volkswagen is committed to co-operating with Numsa to ensure that sound labour relations are re-established throughout the company. We will also look at ways in which the negative effects of the strike are minimised for all parties concerned."
